# Feature: Dash tile — sanity check

<!-- Generated by the project-manager tool from pm.yml. Do not edit by hand; the store is the source of truth. -->

## Goal

Sanity-check candidate mechanic #9 (Dash tile) from Movement Tiles before it is used in real levels. Effect: Stores a dash you spend by moving the same way twice. Unique: a stored dash spent by repeating a direction, not a tile you count from. Useful: save the leap for the hazard or deadline that actually needs it. Source status in the candidate file is 'revised'; it was revised from human review and is now treated as a trial candidate.

## User Story

**As a** player

**I want** stores a dash you spend by moving the same way twice.

**So that** save the leap for the hazard or deadline that actually needs it.

## High-Level Use Case

The player meets Dash tile for the first time in its teaching room (mech-9-dash-tile-room). Teaching moment: First room: the dash tile sits on a straight corridor a player is already walking along. A player who keeps moving in the same direction out of habit spends the stored dash into the far wall and has nothing left for the gap beyond it, which teaches that repeating a direction is the trigger and that the charge is kept by changing direction. The sanity check plays that room, exercises every rule below, and records a replayable session.

## Player-Facing Behavior

- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: Stepping on the tile stores one dash, shown in the HUD
- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: Moving in the same direction twice in a row spends it: the second step travels two tiles and can clear a one-tile hazard or gap
- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: Changing direction keeps the charge, so when and where to spend it is the decision, not counting tiles

## Edge Cases & Rules

- Movement/state stays deterministic: state advances only through the pure step function with recorded t_ms; a recorded session replays to the same end state.
- Restart (R / restart) restores the room to its initial state, including this mechanic.

## UI / Feedback

- The player sees Dash tile's effect happen on its tile(s) exactly as the rules above describe; no hidden state.
- Any counter, inventory or HUD impact follows the rules above; if a rule needs a counter it is shown while it matters (see Open Questions).
- Failure in the teaching room returns the player to the room start / checkpoint for an immediate retry.

## Assets & Level Data Needed

- Level JSON: new Test Level mech-9-dash-tile-room (rows + legend) implementing the teaching moment above.
- Sprites/defs: reuse existing tiles where the mechanic reuses an existing tile; add a new sprite/tile def only if this mechanic introduces a new tile (confirm in the implement task).
- Source: plans/level-design/candidate-mechanics/movement-tiles.yml mechanic #9.
